title: Getting fired from a brass band over buying liquor after funerals
summary: He was fired from a brass band and other bands for refusing to pay for liquor after funerals, and says Kid Howard did the same to him.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: No, that's good. That doesn't matter. We talk about everything on these things.
Find out what things were really like in those days. Yeah.

So I got fired at that band because, you see, like we play a funeral and they finish, uh, like say here, you know. You go pay off where that, two, three blocks at that corner. Oh yeah. Uh, so we can buy the liquor, you see what I mean. They had no barroom, you know, that's paying off. They had to go without. Well, I wouldn't buy no liquor. I bought it once or twice and I told them I ain't doing it no more. Because the job wasn't paying that much. And if you had to take and go make four or five dollars, you know, sweat yourself to them. And then I have to go buy a liquor, nothing to come with don't make sense. So I told them I wasn't going to do it no more. And they fired them. Yeah. Get rid of me. And I got fired out about two or three bands on the counter there. And, uh, Kid Howard did me the same thing. Yeah. Yeah. Boy, I don't know what to tell you. And I had lots of work one time. Yeah. I gave all them fellas work. They never fix me up like I fix them up. But I'm living, you know. They never fix me up. Yeah. And, uh, I used to have, uh, this Maison Blanche annex I just opened. I used to work for them, advertise. He said, go and put us up on that second floor up there. And we played for the customers that come in. Right in the stores.
